LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 1.3.1 WORD CLASSES: COMPOUND NOUNS

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.3: Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes: Compound Nouns
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes: Compound Nouns, part of Strand 1 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 8 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why should we use compound nouns when communicating? 2. How do compound nouns form plurals?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes: Compound Nouns together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and collaboration as the learner works with peers to categorise compound nouns.

● Self-efficacy as the learner shows concerted attention to detail when forming separate and hyphenated compound nouns by

combining two or more words.

● Learning to learn as the learner engages in self- driven tasks while using compound nouns in sentences.

Values:
8

Respect: the learner works in groups to identify the compound nouns in the text

Link to other subjects:

Using compound nouns is linked to using compound words in Kiswahili, German and French.

Suggested Learning Resources:

• Audio recording

• Lists of Categories of compound words
